correctness.rationale: In the presentation with the complement acting by a residue u of exact order m modulo r, every outside element with complement coordinate b not congruent to zero lies in a unique conjugate complement because 1-u^b is invertible modulo r. Hence distinct complements meet trivially and every non-kernel cyclic subgroup lies in one complement. The prime kernel is a leaf, so the cyclic-subgroup graph is exactly the asserted one-point union. The vertex and edge formulas follow by disjoint counting, and the cyclic comparison follows from the standard divisor-lattice edge formula. Strictness uses e(m) at least tau(m)-1 and r at least five. The packaged checker reconstructs all cyclic subgroups and all cover relations for six examples.

value.rationale: The 2023 primary paper explicitly leaves the even-order edge-minimality statement open. The final theorem settles it strictly for a broad and standard infinite class of nonnilpotent solvable groups, namely prime-kernel Frobenius groups with every even cyclic complement of order at least four. It also gives the entire cyclic-subgroup graph as a one-point union, so the result is structural rather than a single inequality or isolated computation.
